_meta.title: Prompt recipes - ready to render, none of them rendered yet
_meta.author: desk research, see craft/INSPIRATION.md
_meta.status_of_this_file: EVERY recipe is status=unrendered and every 'why' is a PREDICTION, not a measurement. This project's own standard, written on the Illustrious checkpoint card: a recommendation is not a measurement. These become facts when someone renders them and looks at them.
_meta.read_first: craft/INSPIRATION.md - Part 2 is where every technique below comes from, Part 3 is the four contradictions the probe recipes exist to settle.
_meta.render_probes_first: The 12 probe_* recipes settle open questions whose answers change the other 48. Render them before anything else. In particular probe_quality_tags decides whether the anime quality string below is right, and one sed fixes all 18 illustration recipes if it is not.

engines.anime: animagine-xl-4.0 (SDXL). DANBOORU TAGS, comma separated, ordered by importance. Despite the name this is the general ILLUSTRATION engine - watercolour, ukiyo-e and oil paint all live here. Vendor settings: 28 steps, cfg 5.0, euler_ancestral, 832x1216 / 1024x1024 / 1216x832.
engines.qwen: Qwen-Image 2512. PROSE sentences, photographic. Cannot be steered off photography by prompt at any cfg - that needs a LoRA. Vendor aspect buckets only: 1328x1328, 1664x928, 928x1664, 1472x1104, 1104x1472, 1584x1056, 1056x1584.

_meta.prompt_field: The 'prompt' field is LITERAL and COMPLETE, including the trailing quality string on anime recipes. Copy and paste it. Nothing is appended at render time.
_meta.negative_field: The 'negative' field is a token resolved from the table below, optionally extended by 'negative_add'. Same convention as studio/styles/*.json.

negatives.@anime: lowres, bad anatomy, bad hands, text, error, missing finger, extra digits, fewer digits, cropped, worst quality, low quality, low score, bad score, average score, signature, watermark, username, blurry, multiple views, photorealistic, 3d, western comic
negatives.@qwen_cfg: low resolution, low quality, deformed limbs, deformed fingers, oversaturated, waxy skin, no facial detail, over-smoothed, artificial AI look, cluttered composition, blurred distorted text

negatives_provenance.@anime: The Animagine XL 4.0 vendor negative (verbatim from the model card) MERGED with the three style-steering terms this project measured for itself - multiple views, photorealistic, 3d, western comic. UNDER TEST: see probe_quality_tags_*.
negatives_provenance.@qwen: A single space, not an empty string - that is what the Qwen-Image repo uses when no negative is wanted. At cfg 1.0 on the Lightning path a negative is inert anyway; this is the honest way to write 'none'.
negatives_provenance.@qwen_cfg: For the 20-step cfg 2.5 path only, where CFG is live. This is an English adaptation of the Chinese negative in the Qwen-Image repo. THE ADAPTATION IS MINE AND UNVERIFIED - the vendor never published an English one.

quality_strings.anime: masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
quality_strings.provenance: Verbatim from the Animagine XL 4.0 model card. NOTE this is NOT what studio/_tools/gallery_gen.py currently uses - it uses 'masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres', where 'very aesthetic' is an Animagine 3.1 token and the 4.0 score scale is absent entirely. probe_quality_tags_a/b/c decides which is right.
quality_strings.qwen: none - CLIP-era quality soup does nothing on a Qwen2.5-VL text encoder (PROMPTING.md). The vendor does recommend one anyway; probe_qwen_magic_a/b tests that disagreement.

constraints_applied_to_every_prompt: Nouns, not adjectives. Objects, materials, named light sources and named framing. Mood is carried by a noun or by a light, never by a mood word.
No style named after an object unless the object appearing in frame is acceptable - the measured noun-as-prop hazard (graffiti put a spray can in the subject's hands).
Every anime recipe states an explicit shot size from the Danbooru ladder, so no recipe silently reproduces the 90px-face failure of full_body at 832x1216.
Resolutions come from the vendor's trained buckets for that engine, never invented.
style / look / place reference real card ids so a recipe composes through studio/compose.py instead of bypassing the layer stack.
Pale styles are paired only with gentle looks - a contrast grade turns a watercolour into mud (STYLE_AND_LAYERS.md).

fields.technique: which finding in INSPIRATION.md this exercises
fields.why: the MECHANISM expected to make it land. A prediction.
fields.risk: the specific way it is expected to fail, so the reviewer knows what to look at
fields.style / look / place: card id in studio/styles, studio/looks, studio/places - or null
fields.settings: steps, cfg, sampler. Omitted keys take the engine default.

recipes.title: Quality probe A - no quality string at all
recipes.prompt: 1girl, solo, cowboy shot, straight-on, standing between tall bookshelves, dark green wool coat, brass buttons, short black hair, grey eyes, reading room, brass desk lamp, dust in the air
recipes.technique: PART 3.1 - quality tokens are adjectives, and the noun rule says adjectives do nothing
recipes.why: The control. If the noun rule holds universally, A B and C are the same image and the whole quality-token tradition is cargo cult on this checkpoint.
recipes.risk: None - this is the baseline. Judge the other two against it.

recipes.title: Quality probe B - the string gallery_gen.py ships today
recipes.prompt: 1girl, solo, cowboy shot, straight-on, standing between tall bookshelves, dark green wool coat, brass buttons, short black hair, grey eyes, reading room, brass desk lamp, dust in the air, masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres
recipes.technique: PART 2.1 - the incumbent string, containing an Animagine 3.1 token
recipes.why: 'very aesthetic' was a real trained label on Animagine 3.1. On 4.0 it may be inert, or worse than inert if it pulls toward the older model's aesthetic.
recipes.risk: May be indistinguishable from A, which would be the finding.

recipes.title: Quality probe C - the Animagine 4.0 vendor string
recipes.prompt: 1girl, solo, cowboy shot, straight-on, standing between tall bookshelves, dark green wool coat, brass buttons, short black hair, grey eyes, reading room, brass desk lamp, dust in the air, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.technique: PART 2.1 - vendor-recommended quality enhancement, verbatim from the model card
recipes.why: Danbooru score tags are not descriptions, they are trained classifier labels attached by rating. If the noun rule needs an exception for trained labels, this is where it shows.
recipes.risk: Score tags may push toward the aesthetic of high-scoring danbooru posts specifically, which is a real style, not neutral quality.

recipes.title: Framing ladder 1/4 - full body, the known-bad case
recipes.prompt: 1boy, solo, male focus, full body, straight-on, standing at a rooftop parapet, black bomber jacket, orange lining, dark red hair, undercut, yellow eyes, city lights below, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 and PART 3.4 - the Danbooru shot-size ladder against the 90px-face measurement
recipes.why: Reproduces the measured failure deliberately: at 832x1216 a full-body head is about 1/8 of frame height, roughly 90px, decided by an 11x11 latent patch.
recipes.risk: This one is supposed to look bad. Crop the head and put the four crops side by side.

recipes.title: Framing ladder 2/4 - cowboy shot, one token cheaper than any other fix
recipes.prompt: 1boy, solo, male focus, cowboy shot, straight-on, standing at a rooftop parapet, black bomber jacket, orange lining, dark red hair, undercut, yellow eyes, city lights below, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 - cowboy shot is the trained tag for a mid-thigh crop
recipes.why: The whole point of the ladder. If the face is materially better here at identical resolution and identical LoRA weight, the cheapest face fix in the project is one token and it costs nothing.
recipes.risk: Costume detail below mid-thigh is lost - which is exactly the composite-sheet tradeoff already measured for photographic sheets.

recipes.title: Framing ladder 3/4 - upper body
recipes.prompt: 1boy, solo, male focus, upper body, straight-on, at a rooftop parapet, black bomber jacket, orange lining, dark red hair, undercut, yellow eyes, city lights below, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 - shot-size ladder
recipes.why: Head now occupies a large fraction of frame height, so the face gets many times the latent area to be decided in.
recipes.risk: Loses the parapet and most of the setting; the place card stops doing any work.

recipes.title: Framing ladder 4/4 - portrait
recipes.prompt: 1boy, solo, male focus, portrait, straight-on, dark red hair, undercut, yellow eyes, black bomber jacket collar, bokeh city lights behind, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 - the tight end of the ladder
recipes.why: Maximum pixels on the face. Establishes the ceiling the other three are measured against.
recipes.risk: Costume and setting both gone. Confirms the measured composite-sheet finding on the illustration engine rather than the photographic one.

recipes.title: Camera-noun probe A - no equipment named
recipes.prompt: A woman in her fifties seated at a kitchen table by a north-facing window, hands around a chipped enamel mug, grey hair cut short, a navy fisherman's jumper, soft daylight from the window falling across one side of her face, the far side of the room in shadow, muted blue and oatmeal palette
recipes.technique: PART 3.3 - control for the camera-brand claim
recipes.why: Baseline with no equipment vocabulary at all. Everything the frame does is coming from subject, light and palette.
recipes.risk: None. Judge B and C against it.

recipes.title: Camera-noun probe B - focal length only
recipes.prompt: A woman in her fifties seated at a kitchen table by a north-facing window, hands around a chipped enamel mug, grey hair cut short, a navy fisherman's jumper, soft daylight from the window falling across one side of her face, the far side of the room in shadow, muted blue and oatmeal palette, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field
recipes.technique: PART 2.6 - focal length, already confirmed to land locally
recipes.why: Focal length is an abstract property, not an object. PROMPTING.md already records that this family lands on Qwen, so B should differ from A in compression and depth of field and in nothing else.
recipes.risk: None expected. If B does not differ from A, the 20-step path is not doing what PROMPTING.md says and that is a bigger finding.

recipes.title: Camera-noun probe C - brand and body named. LOOK FOR A CAMERA IN THE FRAME.
recipes.prompt: A woman in her fifties seated at a kitchen table by a north-facing window, hands around a chipped enamel mug, grey hair cut short, a navy fisherman's jumper, soft daylight from the window falling across one side of her face, the far side of the room in shadow, muted blue and oatmeal palette, shot on a Hasselblad X2D, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field
recipes.technique: PART 3.3 - the contested claim, tested against the measured noun-as-prop hazard
recipes.why: Every Flux guide says naming a body imports its sensor size, dynamic range and colour science. All of them attribute that to the T5 encoder. Qwen-Image does not use T5, it uses Qwen2.5-VL-7B, so the claim transfers only by assumption.
recipes.risk: THE INTERESTING FAILURE: 'Hasselblad X2D' is a noun naming a physical object, and this project has measured that a style named after an object gets the object drawn. A camera on the table, or a photograph of a camera, is the predicted noun-as-prop failure and would be a genuine catch - universal advice being wrong on this stack.

recipes.title: Qwen positive-magic probe A - without the vendor suffix
recipes.prompt: Fishing boats at anchor in a harbour before sunrise, mist lying on the water, wet rope coiled on the stone quay, gulls on the bollards, cold blue light with a thin band of orange at the horizon, 35mm lens
recipes.technique: PART 2.3 - the vendor recommends CLIP-era quality soup that PROMPTING.md says is dead weight
recipes.why: Control. PROMPTING.md states plainly that tag soup does close to nothing on a Qwen2.5-VL encoder and wastes context.
recipes.risk: None.

recipes.title: Qwen positive-magic probe B - with the vendor suffix, verbatim
recipes.prompt: Fishing boats at anchor in a harbour before sunrise, mist lying on the water, wet rope coiled on the stone quay, gulls on the bollards, cold blue light with a thin band of orange at the horizon, 35mm lens, Ultra HD, 4K, cinematic composition.
recipes.technique: PART 2.3 - the Qwen-Image repo's own English 'positive magic', verbatim including the trailing full stop
recipes.why: The people who trained the model append this. The local doc says it does nothing. One of the two is wrong and nobody has looked.
recipes.risk: 'cinematic composition' may widen the frame or add letterbox bars - it is a composition instruction hiding inside a quality string.

recipes.title: North window portrait
recipes.prompt: Head and shoulders of a man in his sixties beside a north-facing studio window, deep lines at the eyes, three days of white stubble, a collarless linen shirt, single soft light source from camera left falling across the face and leaving a triangle of light on the shadow cheek, dark grey seamless backdrop, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, fine skin texture
recipes.technique: PART 2.4 named lighting setup, PART 2.6 focal length, close framing per the face-pixel rule
recipes.why: Rembrandt lighting is described by its effect - the triangle on the shadow cheek - instead of by its name, so the model gets a geometry to draw rather than a term to recognise. Head-and-shoulders framing puts maximum pixels on the face.
recipes.risk: Skin may still go waxy; that is the failure the @qwen_cfg negative is aimed at, and it is the one to check first.

recipes.title: Quinces on a scrubbed table
recipes.prompt: Four quinces on a scrubbed pine table, one cut open showing the grainy pale flesh and dark pips, a knife with a worn wooden handle beside them, grey wool cloth bunched at the edge of the frame, single window light from the left, deep shadow on the right, ochre and grey-green palette, large format, shallow depth of field
recipes.technique: PART 2.5 prompt anatomy - subject, setting, light, lens, palette; every element a noun
recipes.why: Still life is where the noun rule is cleanest: there is nothing in this prompt but objects, a light direction and a palette. Cut fruit gives the model an internal texture to resolve, which is what separates a good still life from a stock photo.
recipes.risk: The cut face of a quince is unusual enough that the model may render an apple or a pear instead. Check the pips.

recipes.title: Board-marked concrete stair
recipes.prompt: A cantilevered concrete stair turning through a top-lit atrium, board marks and tie holes visible in the concrete, a steel handrail worn bright by hands, rainwater staining below a drainage spout, flat overcast light falling from a roof light, no people, 24mm lens, grey and rust palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.6 wide focal length for interiors, PART 2.4 named light source
recipes.why: Board marks, tie holes and a hand-worn rail are three specific nouns that carry the whole brutalist reading without the word brutalist doing any work.
recipes.risk: 'no people' is a negative expressed in the positive prompt; at cfg 2.5 it may be honoured, at cfg 1.0 it will not be. If a figure appears, move it to the negative.

recipes.title: Sea stack, two minute exposure
recipes.prompt: A black basalt sea stack standing off a cliff at dusk, the sea reduced to a smooth grey plane by a two minute exposure, water blurring into mist around the base of the rock, storm cloud shot through with copper light, spray frozen on the wet rock face, long exposure, large format, deep teal and amber palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.6 long exposure; INSPIRATION Part 2.4 - light named by source and colour temperature
recipes.why: 'reduced to a smooth grey plane by a two minute exposure' describes the mechanism rather than naming the technique, which gives the model a specific appearance to produce.
recipes.risk: The model may render motion blur streaks instead of the smooth plane. If so, drop the word blurring.

recipes.title: Sodium light, wet tarmac
recipes.prompt: A terraced street after midnight rain, orange sodium street lamps every thirty metres, the wet tarmac carrying their reflections in long orange smears, a parked estate car beaded with water, one lit upstairs window, halation blooming around every light source, 35mm lens, orange and black palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.4 named practical light sources; halation is the specific artefact that reads as tungsten film
recipes.why: Sodium vapour has a near-monochromatic spectrum, so naming it constrains the palette harder than any colour adjective could. Halation is a named film artefact with a specific look.
recipes.risk: The grade in looks/sodium will push orange again on top of an already orange frame. Check it is not clipping.

recipes.title: Dragonfly wing at 2:1
recipes.prompt: A dragonfly at rest on a reed, photographed at two to one magnification, dew beaded along the veins of the wing, the wing membrane splitting the low sun into faint colour, compound eye filling the left of the frame, background reduced to a wash of green and gold, macro lens, extremely shallow depth of field, focus on the eye
recipes.technique: PART 2.6 macro and depth of field; PART 2.2 focus stated explicitly
recipes.why: Naming the magnification ratio and the focus point gives the model both a scale and a plane. Wing veins and a compound eye are high-frequency structures that reward a 20-step path.
recipes.risk: Insect anatomy - count the wings and the legs. This is the classic place where a beautiful image is quietly wrong.

recipes.title: Heron in the reeds at first light
recipes.prompt: A grey heron standing motionless in shallow water at the edge of a reedbed, neck folded, one foot lifted clear of the surface, mist over the water at first light, reeds behind it going soft, low sun catching the white of the throat, 400mm lens, shallow depth of field, muted green and pewter palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.6 long lens compression; the subject is described by posture, which is a noun-level fact
recipes.why: 'neck folded, one foot lifted clear of the surface' is what a heron actually does, and posture is the thing that separates a real wildlife photograph from a bird-shaped object.
recipes.risk: Long-lens compression may not appear at all; check whether the reeds behind actually separate.

recipes.title: Salt flat from three hundred metres
recipes.prompt: A dried salt flat seen from three hundred metres directly overhead, the crust cracked into a honeycomb of polygons, a single vehicle track crossing the frame diagonally leaving two thin shadows, brine standing pink in the lowest cracks, midday sun, aerial photograph, white and pink palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 camera angle stated as geometry (directly overhead) rather than as a mood
recipes.why: A top-down view removes the horizon, which removes the model's strongest compositional habit and forces it to make a pattern instead. The single track gives the eye somewhere to go.
recipes.risk: The model may reintroduce a horizon. If it does, that is worth writing down - it is the same class of failure as a style card being ignored.

recipes.title: Harbour as a model railway
recipes.prompt: A working container harbour seen from a hillside above, gantry cranes, stacked containers in red blue and rust, a tug crossing the basin leaving a wake, a narrow band of sharp focus across the middle of the frame with everything above and below falling out of focus, tilt-shift lens, high sun, saturated colour
recipes.technique: PART 2.6 tilt-shift, described by its optical signature rather than by the word miniature
recipes.why: The miniature effect is a consequence of a narrow focus band and saturated colour. Describing the band directly is more reliable than asking for 'miniature', which is an adjective and invites the model to draw an actual model.
recipes.risk: The noun-as-prop hazard in miniature: if 'miniature' had been used, expect a toy. It has been avoided deliberately - do not add it back.

recipes.title: Fish market, six in the morning
recipes.prompt: A fish market hall at six in the morning, crushed ice heaped on steel tables, a man in a rubber apron and white boots lifting a crate, breath visible in the cold air, overhead fluorescent tubes throwing flat green-tinted light, wet concrete floor, water running to a drain, 35mm lens, no flash
recipes.technique: PART 2.6 the 35mm documentary register; PART 2.4 fluorescent named as a source with a colour cast
recipes.why: Fluorescent tubes have a green cast that no colour adjective would produce as reliably. 'no flash' is a photographic constraint the model has seen described in captions.
recipes.risk: Hands holding a crate. Check the fingers before anything else.

recipes.title: Editorial, one hard strobe
recipes.prompt: A model in a scarlet wool coat with exaggerated shoulders standing against a cyclorama painted deep ultramarine, one bare hard strobe from camera right casting a sharp shadow onto the wall behind, no fill light, hair pulled back flat, full length, 50mm lens, red and blue palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.4 - source, quality, direction, and the absence of fill stated explicitly
recipes.why: 'one bare hard strobe from camera right' plus 'no fill light' is a complete lighting specification. The sharp shadow on the cyclorama is the visible proof it landed - it is a checkable outcome, not a vibe.
recipes.risk: Full length framing means a small face. That is acceptable here because the coat is the subject, but do not reuse this framing for a character sheet.

recipes.title: Glass bottle on wet slate
recipes.prompt: A heavy faceted glass bottle with a brushed steel cap standing on wet black slate, water beaded on the slate around it, a single strip softbox behind and above throwing a long vertical highlight down one facet, black background, the bottle refracting a band of cold blue, product photograph, 100mm lens, focus stacked
recipes.technique: PART 2.4 named modifier (strip softbox) with position, which is what product lighting actually is
recipes.why: A strip softbox produces a specific long thin highlight, and naming the highlight tells the model what to draw. Focus stacking is a caption term associated with front-to-back sharp product work.
recipes.risk: Glass and refraction are where diffusion models invent geometry. Look along the edges of the facets.

recipes.title: Infrared woodland
recipes.prompt: A beech wood photographed on infrared film, the foliage rendered chalk white, the trunks near black, the sky dark and almost without cloud, a path of pale grass running away between the trees, high contrast, infrared photograph, white and near-black palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.5 medium named last, effect described first
recipes.why: Infrared has one unmistakable signature - white foliage against a dark sky - and stating that signature as fact does more than naming the film stock.
recipes.risk: The model may simply desaturate rather than invert the tonal relationship. If the leaves are grey rather than white, it did not land.

recipes.title: Dome open to the winter sky
recipes.prompt: The interior of an observatory dome with the shutter open on a winter night, the white tube of a refracting telescope angled up through the gap, a red work lamp on the floor throwing the only warm light, star trails visible through the opening, steel walkway, cold breath, long exposure, red and steel blue palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.4 practical light as the sole source; INSPIRATION 2.4 caveat - darkness comes from the grade
recipes.why: A single red work lamp is a strong compositional constraint and a real astronomy practice. The star trails through the shutter gap give the long exposure something visible to prove itself on.
recipes.risk: Prompting for darkness does nothing - measured, luma 170 to 161. If this is not dark enough, looks/moonlit is what fixes it, not more words.

recipes.title: Victorian glasshouse, morning
recipes.prompt: The inside of a Victorian glasshouse in the morning, white-painted cast iron ribs curving overhead, condensation running down the glass, staged tiers of terracotta pots, a brick path with moss in the joints, sunlight coming through the misted glass in visible shafts, 24mm lens, green and terracotta palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.6 24mm for interiors; PART 2.4 volumetric shafts named as a consequence of misted glass
recipes.why: The shafts are motivated - misted glass is why they are visible - which tends to produce more coherent volumetrics than asking for god rays directly.
recipes.risk: 24mm plus curved iron ribs is a lot of repeating structure. Check the ribs stay parallel and do not braid.

recipes.title: Supercell over wheat
recipes.prompt: A rotating supercell thunderstorm over flat wheat country in late afternoon, the wall cloud lowered and striated like a stack of plates, green-tinged light beneath the base, wheat bent flat by the inflow, a single grain elevator on the horizon for scale, dust lifting off a dirt road, 35mm lens, green and bronze palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.5 anatomy; every dramatic element is a physical noun, never an adjective
recipes.why: 'striated like a stack of plates' and 'green-tinged light beneath the base' are what a supercell actually looks like. The grain elevator is there purely to give scale, which is what makes a big sky read as big.
recipes.risk: Sky drama is where the model most wants to over-deliver. If it looks like an album cover, cut the palette clause.

recipes.title: Backstreet, signs as the only light
recipes.prompt: A narrow backstreet at night lit only by the shop signs along it, a magenta tube sign and a cold green one facing each other across the alley, steam from a floor vent catching both colours, air conditioning units bracketed to the wall, puddles carrying broken reflections of the tubes, a bicycle chained to a downpipe, 35mm lens, magenta and green palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.4 practical sources named individually with their own colours
recipes.why: Naming two opposed sign colours and putting steam between them gives the model a reason for coloured volumetrics, and the puddles give it a second surface to repeat them on.
recipes.risk: Signs will try to render text. If letterforms appear and are garbage, either accept them out of focus or move to the 20-step path and put a real string in quotes.

recipes.title: Kelp forest from below
recipes.prompt: Looking up through a giant kelp forest towards the surface, the stipes rising in columns, blades turning slowly in the swell, sunlight breaking through the canopy in shifting shafts, a shoal of small silver fish crossing between the columns, particulate suspended in the water, wide angle lens, green and gold palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 camera angle as geometry (looking up); PART 2.4 shafts motivated by a canopy
recipes.why: Upward angle plus columns is a strong composition the model has seen many times in captioned dive photography. Suspended particulate is the detail that makes water read as water rather than as green air.
recipes.risk: looks/underwater will add its own colour cast on top of the prompted one. Check they are not fighting.

recipes.title: One tree, a lot of snow
recipes.prompt: A single bare oak standing in an unbroken snowfield under a white sky, no horizon line visible where the snow meets the cloud, the tree small and placed left of centre, animal tracks crossing the lower right of the frame, flat diffuse light, no shadows, 50mm lens, white and grey-brown palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.8 - minimal composition stated as facts about the frame rather than as 'negative space'
recipes.why: 'placed left of centre', 'no horizon line visible', 'no shadows' are three checkable statements about the picture. This is the honest version of the composition vocabulary the trend guides recommend and never test.
recipes.risk: Flat white is where a model reaches for contrast it was not asked for. If a blue sky appears, the prompt lost.

recipes.title: Hands on a wheel
recipes.prompt: Close on a potter's hands closing the rim of a tall cylinder on a wheel, slip running over the knuckles and down the wrists, the clay wall thin enough to show the light through at the lip, a bucket of grey water beside the wheel, low afternoon sun from a side window, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, ochre and grey palette
recipes.technique: close framing per the face-pixel rule, applied to hands instead of a face
recipes.why: Hands are the other structure that fails when it is small. Close framing gives them the same pixel budget a portrait gives a face, which is the whole argument of the fix order.
recipes.risk: Hands, deliberately, at maximum size. This is the recipe that will most clearly show whether the 20-step path is competent at them. Count the fingers.

recipes.title: Launderette, Sunday
recipes.prompt: A launderette on a Sunday afternoon, a row of front-loading machines with three of them running, a woman in a yellow raincoat reading a paperback on a moulded plastic chair, folded towels stacked on a formica table, daylight through a steamed front window, linoleum floor, 35mm lens, yellow and pale blue palette
recipes.technique: PART 4.1 - ordinary subject matter, which is what the data says actually gets looked at
recipes.why: A specific mundane scene with named objects gives the model no room to reach for spectacle. The yellow raincoat is a single saturated note in an otherwise pale frame, which is a composition device made of a noun.
recipes.risk: The paperback will try to have text on it. Leave it out of focus or give it a real string.

recipes.title: Forge at the moment of the strike
recipes.prompt: A blacksmith bringing a hammer down on a bar of steel at orange heat, scale flying off the work as bright sparks, the anvil face polished mirror bright, the forge mouth glowing behind, the rest of the workshop in near darkness lit only by the work itself, leather apron, 50mm lens, orange and black palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.4 - the subject is the light source, which is the strongest possible motivation
recipes.why: When the hot steel is the only light, every shadow in the frame is explained by it. That is a much stronger constraint than any lighting adjective, and it is why forge photographs look the way they do.
recipes.risk: Sparks are easy and the swing is hard. Look at the shoulder and the hammer haft, not at the sparks.

recipes.title: Watercolour moorland
recipes.prompt: no humans, scenery, wide shot, moorland, heather, drystone wall crossing the slope, low cloud on the ridge, watercolor (medium), traditional media, wet-on-wet, bleeding colours, pale palette, soft edges, paper texture, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: cel shading, flat colour, opaque paint, heavy black outlines, digital art, 3d
recipes.technique: the strongest measured style card in the library, on its own engine, paired with a gentle look
recipes.why: watercolour is measured at 92.1 from control on the anime path and the trained tag is the American spelling with the danbooru disambiguator - watercolor (medium) - which is what this prompt uses. Landscape with no figure removes the anatomy risk entirely and lets the medium be the subject.
recipes.risk: The card is explicit that a contrast grade destroys this style; looks/memory is on its suits_looks list, looks/noir and looks/night are not. Do not swap the look.

recipes.title: Shin-hanga, rain on a bridge
recipes.prompt: 1girl, solo, cowboy shot, from behind, walking across a wooden bridge in rain, oil-paper umbrella, dark kimono, wooden geta, river below, rain drawn as fine parallel lines, ukiyo-e, shin-hanga, woodblock print, flat colour areas, visible key block outline, limited palette, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: gradient shading, digital painting, photorealistic, 3d
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 shot size and camera angle as trained tags; medium described by its printing mechanics
recipes.why: Rain as fine parallel lines and a visible key block are the two things that make a woodblock print read as printed rather than painted. From behind removes the face, which removes the face problem.
recipes.risk: Umbrella ribs and geta are both fiddly. Check the ribs converge on one point.

recipes.title: Ink wash bamboo
recipes.prompt: no humans, scenery, bamboo grove, mist between the culms, a single sparrow on a stem, ink wash painting, sumi-e, monochrome, greyscale, visible brush strokes, dry brush, large areas of bare paper, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: colour, cel shading, heavy outlines, digital art, 3d
recipes.technique: restraint as a noun - 'large areas of bare paper' names the emptiness as a material
recipes.why: Ink wash is defined by what is not painted. Naming bare paper as an element gives the model a positive instruction to leave space, which 'minimalist' would not.
recipes.risk: The model will want to fill the frame. If the paper disappears, this style needs a stronger negative rather than more words.

recipes.title: Oil portrait, impasto highlights
recipes.prompt: 1boy, solo, male focus, portrait, three-quarter view, an old man with a white beard, dark coat, plain dark background, single warm light on one side of the face, oil painting, visible brush strokes, impasto highlights, canvas weave showing through the thin darks, cracked varnish, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: photorealistic, digital art, smooth shading, 3d, watercolor
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 portrait framing plus three-quarter view; the measured fact that the illustration engine does oil paint
recipes.why: Impasto, canvas weave and cracked varnish are three physical properties of an oil painting as an object, not adjectives about painting. Portrait framing gives the face the pixels the fix order demands.
recipes.risk: Cracked varnish may be read as damage to the image rather than to the paint. If the whole frame gets distressed, drop that clause.

recipes.title: Gouache kitchen still life
recipes.prompt: no humans, still life, a chipped blue teapot, three lemons, a striped cloth, a kitchen window behind, gouache, opaque matte paint, flat blocks of colour, visible edges where one block meets another, slight paper texture, limited palette, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: transparent washes, watercolor, glossy, photorealistic, 3d
recipes.technique: gouache defined against watercolour by opacity - the negative carries the distinction
recipes.why: Gouache and watercolour share a vocabulary and differ in one property: gouache is opaque. Stating opacity in the positive and transparency in the negative is the whole recipe.
recipes.risk: Very likely to drift toward watercolour, which is the strongest card in the library and a strong attractor. Compare against illus_watercolour_moor.

recipes.title: Art nouveau panel
recipes.prompt: 1girl, solo, upper body, straight-on, long copper hair worked into flowing curves, a robe of pale green, surrounded by a border of stylised irises and whiplash stems, a circular halo of ornament behind the head, art nouveau, mucha, flat colour, heavy contour line of even weight, decorative border, muted palette, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: gradient shading, photorealistic, 3d, heavy shadow
recipes.technique: PART 4.2 overlap - decorative illustration; PART 2.2 upper body framing
recipes.why: The whiplash stem, the even-weight contour and the circular ornament behind the head are the three structural signatures of the style, all nouns. The halo device also solves the background.
recipes.risk: Ornate borders are where a model repeats itself into mush at the corners. Look at the corners.

recipes.title: Ligne claire street scene
recipes.prompt: multiple girls, multiple boys, wide shot, a busy market street, awnings, crates of fruit, a delivery bicycle, ligne claire, clear line, uniform line weight, flat unshaded colour, no hatching, no cast shadows, strong local colour, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: hatching, cross hatching, gradient shading, cast shadow, photorealistic, 3d, sketchy lines
recipes.technique: PART 4.1 - line character is the axis the market is actually buying
recipes.why: Ligne claire is defined by three absences - no hatching, no gradients, no cast shadows - and one presence, uniform line weight. All four are stated. This is the cleanest test in the set of whether the engine can be held to a line discipline.
recipes.risk: Crowd scene at wide shot means many small faces, all of them bad. That is expected and acceptable here because the line is the subject; do not read this as a face failure.

recipes.title: Screentone, last carriage
recipes.prompt: 1girl, solo, cowboy shot, from side, sitting alone in the last carriage of a night train, school bag on the seat beside her, window showing black outside with her own reflection, monochrome, greyscale, manga, screentone, halftone dots, speed lines absent, heavy black spotting, white gutters, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: colour, photorealistic, 3d, gradient shading
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 shot size and angle; the medium named by its printing artefacts
recipes.why: Screentone is literally a dot pattern. Naming halftone dots and heavy black spotting asks for the artefact rather than the aesthetic, and the reflection in the window gives the composition a second figure for free.
recipes.risk: 'speed lines absent' is a negative in the positive prompt; if speed lines appear, move it. Reflections are also where geometry goes wrong - check she faces the right way in the glass.

recipes.title: Impact frame
recipes.prompt: 1boy, solo, male focus, cowboy shot, dutch angle, from below, mid-swing with a wooden staff, coat flaring outward, dust kicked up in a ring at the feet, smear frame, motion lines radiating from the impact point, limited palette of two colours plus white, hard black shadow shapes, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: static pose, photorealistic, 3d, soft shading
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 dutch angle and from below as trained tags; motion described as animation artefacts
recipes.why: Smear frames, radiating lines and a dust ring are the drawn conventions for impact. Asking for the conventions is more reliable than asking for 'dynamic', which is the adjective the noun rule says will do nothing.
recipes.risk: A staff crossing the body is a limb-count hazard. Check the arms.

recipes.title: Orchard in late summer
recipes._look_note: golden is on the gentle end; do not swap to a contrast grade or the painted background goes muddy
recipes.prompt: 1girl, solo, wide shot, from side, walking between rows of old apple trees carrying a wicker basket, windfalls in the long grass, a ladder leaning in one tree, low sun through the leaves, painted background, soft cel shading, hand-painted clouds, warm green and gold palette, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: photorealistic, 3d, harsh outlines, dark palette
recipes.technique: PART 4.2 overlap - pastoral illustration is on every trend list; PART 2.4 low sun through foliage
recipes.why: A painted background with cel-shaded figures is the actual production technique being asked for, and naming both halves separately is more precise than naming a studio.
recipes.risk: Wide shot means a small face again. Accepted deliberately - the orchard is the subject. If the face matters, this becomes a cowboy shot.

recipes.title: Chibi, waiting for the spin cycle
recipes.prompt: 1girl, solo, chibi, full body, straight-on, two head tall proportions, oversized head, tiny hands, sitting on a plastic chair swinging her feet above the floor, a washing machine mid-cycle behind her, a basket of socks, thick outline, flat colour, simple shading, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: realistic proportions, photorealistic, 3d, detailed anatomy
recipes.technique: the one case where full_body is correct - chibi proportions put the head at nearly half the figure
recipes.why: Chibi inverts the face-pixel problem: at two heads tall the head occupies half the figure, so full_body framing gives the face more pixels than upper_body would on a realistic figure. Worth having one recipe in the set that proves the rule is about pixels and not about the tag.
recipes.risk: The proportion instruction may only partly land, giving an uncanny three-head figure. Measure the head against the body.

recipes.title: Pixel art arcade
recipes.prompt: no humans, pixel art, a row of arcade cabinets seen from a low three-quarter view, glowing marquee panels, a stool tipped against one cabinet, carpet with a geometric pattern, limited palette of sixteen colours, visible square pixels, dithering in the gradients, hard edges, black outline, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: anti-aliasing, smooth gradients, photorealistic, 3d, blurry
recipes.technique: PART 4.2 - retro-computing nostalgia; the medium named by its constraints
recipes.why: Dithering and a stated palette size are what actually make pixel art read as pixel art. Anti-aliasing in the negative is the specific enemy.
recipes.risk: SDXL at 1024 will usually produce pixel-art-flavoured smoothness rather than a true pixel grid. If the pixels are not square and aligned, this is a downscale-and-quantise job in post, not a prompt job - and that is a useful thing to have proved.

recipes.title: Woodcut wolf
recipes.prompt: no humans, a wolf standing among pine trunks looking back over its shoulder, woodcut print, relief print, black ink on cream paper, bold gouged lines, white cuts through solid black, parallel hatching for the mid tones, rough plate edge, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: colour, gradient shading, photorealistic, 3d, fine pen lines
recipes.technique: PART 4.1 line character; relief printing described by the physical act of cutting
recipes.why: In a woodcut the white marks are the cuts and the black is what remains, which is the opposite of drawing. Saying 'white cuts through solid black' asks for that inversion directly.
recipes.risk: May produce a black-and-white drawing rather than a print. The plate edge is the tell - if there is no edge, it drew rather than printed.

recipes.title: Illuminated manuscript page
recipes.prompt: no humans, a manuscript page on vellum, a large decorated initial letter filled with interlace, a hare and a hound chasing through the marginal vine scroll, burnished gold leaf catching the light, lapis blue and vermilion pigments, ruled text lines, worn edges, illuminated manuscript, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: photorealistic, 3d, modern typography, perspective, cast shadow
recipes.technique: PART 4.1 - a medium the library owns and has never shown
recipes.why: Marginalia with animals, an interlaced initial and named historical pigments are all specific nouns from the real tradition. 'perspective' in the negative matters - the style predates it.
recipes.risk: The ruled text lines will attract garbled letterforms. On this engine that is acceptable as texture; if it is distracting, remove the ruled lines clause.

recipes.title: Persian miniature garden
recipes.prompt: multiple girls, wide shot, a walled garden with a water channel down the centre, cypress and flowering almond, figures in patterned robes seated on a carpet, birds in the branches, persian miniature, flat perspective with the ground plane tilted up, no cast shadows, lapis and turquoise and gold, fine brushwork, decorative border, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: linear perspective, cast shadow, photorealistic, 3d, western painting
recipes.technique: the defining formal property named directly - the tilted ground plane
recipes.why: What makes a Persian miniature is the refusal of vanishing-point perspective: the ground tilts up so the whole garden is visible at once. Naming that geometry is the difference between the real thing and a fantasy illustration with nice colours.
recipes.risk: SDXL has an extremely strong perspective prior. If the ground plane recedes normally, the style did not land and no amount of colour vocabulary will fix it.

recipes.title: Gongbi crane and pine
recipes.prompt: no humans, a red-crowned crane standing beneath a pine branch, gongbi painting, fine outline brushwork, every feather drawn individually, layered transparent colour washes inside the outlines, silk ground, plain pale background, seal stamp in the corner, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: loose brushwork, ink wash, sumi-e, photorealistic, 3d, heavy shadow
recipes.technique: gongbi defined against ink wash - meticulous outline versus loose wash
recipes.why: Gongbi and sumi-e are opposite poles of the same tradition and the library has both. Putting ink wash in the negative is the cleanest way to hold the model on the meticulous side.
recipes.risk: Feather counts. Zoom into the wing - individually drawn feathers is a claim the render either honours or fakes.

recipes.title: Risograph community poster
recipes.prompt: no humans, a poster of a hillside with pylons marching over the ridge, risograph print, two ink layers of fluorescent pink and teal, visible misregistration between the layers where they overlap, coarse halftone dots, ink smudging at one edge, uncoated paper, flat shapes, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: full colour, photorealistic, 3d, gradient shading, clean print
recipes.technique: PART 4.2 lo-fi trend overlap; the medium named by its defects
recipes.why: Risograph is loved for its faults - misregistration, coarse dots, smudging. Asking for the faults by name is the entire recipe, and it is a good demonstration that a defect is a noun.
recipes.risk: Misregistration is a subtle offset the model may ignore entirely. If the two layers align perfectly, it produced a two-colour illustration, not a riso.

recipes.title: Concept art, hangar bay
recipes.prompt: 1boy, solo, male focus, wide shot, from below, a technician in an orange hi-vis vest standing on a gantry beside the shoulder of a grounded mecha, scale given by the size of the hatch beside him, cable looms hanging from an open access panel, overhead sodium work lamps, wet floor, concept art, painterly rendering, industrial detail, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: photorealistic, 3d render, clean, empty background
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 from below for scale; scale established by a named human-sized reference
recipes.why: Scale in concept art comes from putting a known-size object next to an unknown-size one. The hatch and the technician are that reference; without them a giant machine reads as a small model.
recipes.risk: The figure is small at wide shot, so the face will be poor. That is correct for this image - the mecha is the subject - and is the recipe where a face-detail pass would be the wrong spend.

recipes.title: Linocut harbour
recipes.prompt: no humans, fishing boats against a quay, cranes behind, linocut print, two blocks printed in black and burnt orange, broad gouged marks, rounded cut ends where the tool lifted, uneven ink coverage showing the paper through, deckled edge, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: fine detail, photorealistic, 3d, gradient shading, digital art
recipes.technique: PART 4.1 line character; distinguishing lino from woodcut by tool marks
recipes.why: Lino cuts wider and rounder than wood because the material has no grain. 'rounded cut ends where the tool lifted' is the specific mark that separates the two, and having both in the set makes the comparison legible.
recipes.risk: Likely to be near-identical to illus_woodcut_wolf. If it is, that is a real finding about the resolution of the style library and should be written on both cards.

recipes.title: Storybook attic
recipes.prompt: 1girl, solo, upper body, from side, a child sitting up in bed under a sloped attic ceiling with a candle on an upturned crate, a cat asleep on the quilt, a moth at the skylight, storybook illustration, ink line with watercolour wash, cross hatching in the shadows, warm limited palette, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: photorealistic, 3d, digital painting, harsh contrast
recipes.technique: PART 2.2 upper body framing on a child subject; PART 2.4 single candle as motivated light
recipes.why: Ink line plus watercolour wash is a specific technique, not a genre. One candle motivates every shadow in a small space, and the moth at the skylight gives the eye a second point of interest without adding a second light.
recipes.risk: Children's faces are the hardest case on any engine. upper_body is the minimum framing that gives it a chance.

recipes.title: Pointillist meadow
recipes.prompt: 1girl, solo, wide shot, from behind, standing in a summer meadow with her back to the viewer, a straw hat, tall grass to the waist, pointillism, painted entirely in separate dots of pure colour, no blended edges, complementary orange and violet dots side by side in the shadows, visible canvas between the dots, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: blended brushwork, smooth shading, photorealistic, 3d, outlines
recipes.technique: optical mixing described as a physical arrangement of dots
recipes.why: Pointillism is a colour theory made physical - complementary dots placed side by side rather than mixed. Naming the pair that goes in the shadows is the instruction that separates it from generic stippling.
recipes.risk: SDXL tends to render dots as texture over a normally-painted image rather than as the image itself. Zoom in: if there is a smooth painting under the dots, it failed.

recipes.title: Papercut forest, six layers
recipes.prompt: no humans, a forest built from six layers of cut paper set one behind another, each layer a flat silhouette in a slightly different green, visible cut edges, soft drop shadow where each layer sits above the next, a paper moon in the furthest layer, shadow box, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres
recipes.negative_add: painted, photorealistic, 3d render, gradient shading, texture
recipes.technique: depth expressed as a countable number of physical layers
recipes.why: Saying six layers gives the model a countable structure instead of an atmospheric one, and the drop shadow between layers is the cue that makes flat shapes read as stacked paper.
recipes.risk: The count will probably not be exactly six. That is fine; what matters is whether the layers are separated by shadow or merely by colour.

recipes.title: Enamel shop sign
recipes.prompt: A vintage enamel shop sign bolted to a brick wall, the sign reads "NORTHWIND SUPPLY CO." in cream serif lettering on deep green, chipped enamel showing rust at the bolt holes, a hairline crack across one corner, flat overcast daylight, 50mm lens straight on to the wall
recipes.technique: PART 2.3 and PART 2.5 - literal string in quotation marks, typeface described by character not by name
recipes.why: Text is Qwen 2512's headline capability and quoting the string is the documented way to get it rendered rather than described. Describing the letterforms as cream serif rather than naming a font gives the model a property it can draw.
recipes.risk: Long strings and multiple text elements are where the 4-step path first degrades - hence 20 steps here. Read every letter.

recipes.title: Battered paperback cover
recipes.prompt: A battered 1970s science fiction paperback lying face up on a formica table, the cover shows a lone figure before a ringed planet, the title reads "THE LONG COUNT" in heavy condensed sans lettering across the top, creased spine, yellowed page edges, a coffee ring on the corner of the table, window light from the left, 50mm lens
recipes.technique: PART 4.2 retro-future trend overlap; PART 2.3 quoted string
recipes.why: The book is a physical object photographed on a table, which is a scene Qwen is at home in, and the cover art becomes an image-within-an-image the model can stylise without being asked to leave photography - which it cannot do anyway.
recipes.risk: Two competing text opportunities - title and author line. Only one string is specified; if an invented author name appears in garbage letterforms, specify it or crop it.

recipes.title: Letterpress gig poster
recipes.prompt: A letterpress poster pinned to a plywood wall, the poster reads "TUESDAY NIGHTS" in large wood type across the middle with a thick rule above and below it, printed in black and a single warm red on butcher paper, visible bite where the type pressed into the paper, ink slightly heavier at the edges of each letter, one drawing pin at each corner, flat frontal light
recipes.technique: PART 2.3 quoted string; the printing method named by its physical impression
recipes.why: The bite of wood type into paper is a raised-and-recessed texture, a physical fact a photographic model can render. Two-colour and rules keep the layout simple enough for the text to survive.
recipes.risk: Wood type has irregular letterforms by nature, so a slightly wrong letter may read as authentic. Do not let that excuse a misspelling - check the string.

recipes.title: Split-flap departure board
recipes.prompt: A split-flap departure board in a station concourse, the top row reads "DELAYED" in white on black, the rows below half-flipped mid-update with letters caught between characters, the mechanism visible behind the slats, fluorescent light from above, a blurred commuter passing beneath, 50mm lens, black and white and amber palette
recipes.technique: PART 2.3 quoted string with a deliberate excuse for imperfect text elsewhere
recipes.why: The half-flipped rows are the clever part: they give the model licence to produce partial letterforms in the rows that are not specified, which converts the model's characteristic text failure into the subject of the photograph.
recipes.risk: If even the specified row comes out wrong the trick fails and the whole image is unusable. That row is the only thing to check.
